clue.text: Bomb exploding caught rear

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the thud of a bomb going off

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the rump is the hindquarters

explanation.surface: A bomb goes off just as someone is caught from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A crump is the heavy thudding sound of a shell or bomb bursting, and by extension the explosion itself.

clue.text: Scout breaking into college cupboard? Not one eager to work overtime!

definitions.text: Not one eager to work overtime!

indicators.note: something breaking into a thing ends up lodged inside it, splitting it in two

blocks.note: C is a standard abbreviation for college
a locker is a small lockable cupboard
a scout keeps watch; watch here is a lookout or sentinel

explanation.surface: A boy scout bursts into a college cupboard, while somebody grumbles about staff who down tools on the dot.
explanation.walkthrough: The scout splits the college cupboard in two. The question mark and exclamation flag the definition as a jokey description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock-watcher keeps an eye on the time, waiting to leave the moment the working day is over, so is the reverse of keen for extra hours.

clue.text: Cracks upsetting Marie

indicators.note: upsetting something knocks it over and throws it into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that cracks is upsetting a woman called Marie.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimae is the plural of rima, a long narrow cleft or fissure, as in anatomy or on the lunar surface.

clue.text: Contrary to current press release, tremble about losing leader

indicators.note: losing its leader means the word for tremble drops its opening letter
about means going round, so the shortened word wraps around the release

blocks.note: quiver means tremble; its first letter goes
PR, public relations, is what issues press releases

explanation.surface: Someone at odds with a current press release is trembling about losing their party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads like topical news, but it is the flow of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upriver means travelling towards the source, against the direction the stream's current flows.

clue.text: Hitched, as one who was to Willis B

definitions.text: as one who was to Willis B
definitions.note: a punning description: married to Demi Moore

blocks.note: first meaning: tied up, as a boat is to a quay

blocks.clueFragment: as one who was to Willis B
blocks.note: second meaning: Bruce Willis was married to the actress Demi Moore, so he was jokingly Moore-d

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitched' first reads as married, which is the joke; the answer means tied up, and its pun splits it as MOORE plus D, as if Willis had been wedded to a Moore.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored boat is tied fast to a buoy or quay, just as a hitched horse is tied to a post.

clue.text: Teller of epic tales from Senegal about lizards

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the country's code goes round the reptiles

blocks.note: SN is the country code for Senegal
Agama is a genus of Old World lizards

explanation.surface: A West African storyteller recounts epic tales about lizards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sagaman is a reciter or composer of sagas, the long heroic narratives of Norse tradition.

clue.text: End of stage thrust exploited to get one closer?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
something exploited is worked on and put to new use, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the final letter of the word stage
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor exploits a thrust stage's end to deliver a better closing number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One closer?' reads like an improved finale; it is a thing that closes, such as a window cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutter is a hinged panel or camera device that closes off a window or lens, so it is literally something that shuts.

clue.text: Group's outsider possibly providing trail snack

indicators.note: an outsider sits at the edge, so either end letter of the word qualifies

blocks.note: one outside letter of the word group
possibly suggests an alternative, the word or
the other outside letter of the word group

explanation.surface: A hiking group's odd one out might be handing round snacks on the trail.
explanation.walkthrough: Either outer letter of 'group' is its outsider, so the clue reads G or P, giving the answer letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorp is the American name for trail mix, a blend of nuts, raisins and chocolate eaten by hikers for energy.

clue.text: Band of brothers, not all dynamic usually

indicators.note: not all of these words are used, only a run of letters lying across them

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A group of brothers who are, as a rule, not all go-getters.
explanation.walkthrough: Amicus was a large British trade union, later merged into Unite; union members traditionally call one another brothers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union is a body of workers who address each other as brother, so a fraternal band fits this one.

clue.text: One championing innovation lots moved in to copy

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted about out of their written order
in places the shuffled letters inside the word for copy

blocks.note: to ape is to imitate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A champion of new ideas drafts in plenty of people to imitate it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a zealous advocate or early supporter of a new cause or idea, by extension from the first followers of Christ.

clue.text: Form of RSI? It is following start of niggle in most of tendon

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
most of a word means nearly all of it, so its final letter is cut
following tells us the phrase it is follows goes after everything else

blocks.note: the first letter of niggle
taken as written
tendon without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a repetitive strain injury that starts as a niggle in the tendon.
explanation.walkthrough: RSI is repetitive strain injury. The answer is a jokey coinage from the games console brand plus the medical suffix for inflammation, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendoitis is the informal name for thumb and wrist pain caused by long sessions on handheld games consoles, a kind of repetitive strain injury.

clue.text: Kiss given by nasty smoocher (not the first) causing colour-ing in the dairy?

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter of the word is dropped
nasty suggests something spoilt or messed about, so the remaining letters are shuffled

blocks.note: Chambers gives lip as a verb meaning to touch with the lips, to kiss
smoocher without its first letter

explanation.surface: An unwelcome kiss from a creep makes a dairymaid blush.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'colour-ing' hints that this is a pigment, not blushing; the dairy is where it is found, in butter fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lipochrome is a fat-soluble pigment, such as the carotenoids that give butter and cream their yellow tint.

clue.text: Recipe No. I, what Aussie has on his plate?

definitions.text: what Aussie has on his plate?

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions
number one, oneself: the ego is the I

explanation.surface: A cookery book lists its first recipe, and an Australian tucks into what is on his plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The plate is not for food but the number plate of a car; rego is Australian slang for vehicle registration.
explanation.definitionFit: Rego is the Australian short form of registration, and a car's registration number is displayed on its number plate.

clue.text: Ornaments may be set out on it, following silly urge I assume

definitions.text: Ornaments may be set out on it

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so these letters come out in a confused order
following places the word for assume after the jumbled letters

blocks.note: taken as written
to don clothes is to put them on, to assume them

explanation.surface: Someone guesses where trinkets will be displayed, following a foolish impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: A gueridon is a small, ornately carved round table or stand, the kind on which vases or knick-knacks are placed.

clue.text: I'll be taken in by eccentric Scottish tinker

indicators.note: taken in by means received inside, so the word for eccentric holds the I

blocks.note: a card is an odd, amusing person
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits they'll be fooled by a peculiar travelling tinker from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll' splits into the letter I and a link: I will be taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: Caird is a Scots word for a travelling tinker or vagrant.

clue.text: Stingy, I've dismissed price

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so those letters leave the word for stingy

blocks.note: costive can mean niggardly or tight-fisted
the letters removed

explanation.surface: A mean-spirited boss boasts of having sacked someone over the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: Costive is best known as constipated, but Chambers also gives it the sense mean or stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cost and price both name the amount of money that must be paid for something.

clue.text: Velocity in boat (flat-bottomed) giving chance for Jock

indicators.note: in places one item inside the other

blocks.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge, used on the Tyne
V is the symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: Speed in a flat-bottomed boat gives a Scotsman his opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Kevel is a Scots word for a lot cast to decide something, and so for one's fortune or chance.

clue.text: Salt at sea let auto

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An old sailor at sea lets out a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' first suggests an old sailor, which suits 'at sea'; it is a chemical salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A toluate is a salt or ester of toluic acid, so it is a salt in the chemical sense.

clue.text: We scattered seeds round centre of tilth, typical of best gardens

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, the only one kept
scattered things are thrown in all directions, so these letters lose their order
round means surrounding, so the scattered letters go about the kept letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the middle letter of tilth

explanation.surface: Gardeners sow seeds around the middle of a fine tilled bed, as the best gardeners do.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-kept gardens are free of weeds, so weedless describes what is typical of them.

clue.text: With furrows to cleave turned up speed

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to axe is to cleave or chop
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A ploughman with furrows to split turns up the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Exarate is a botanical and zoological term for something grooved or marked with furrows.

clue.text: Man in e.g. Cape Town entering markets for African music

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the word for man sits inside the word for markets

blocks.note: souks are Arab street markets
ou is South African slang for a man or chap

explanation.surface: A man in Cape Town browses the markets for African records.
explanation.definitionFit: Soukous is a dance music from Congo, popular across central and east Africa, rooted in Congolese rumba.

clue.text: Rust-red colouring in work, international according to art circles

indicators.note: circles means goes round, so the phrase for according to art surrounds the rest

blocks.note: s.a. abbreviates the Latin secundum artem, according to art
taken as written
op. is the abbreviation for opus, a work
I is an abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A rust-red pigment appears in a work of international standing, according to the art world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art circles' looks like a phrase for the art world; circles is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinopia is a reddish-brown earth pigment, used for the underdrawing of frescoes, named after Sinope on the Black Sea.

clue.text: Taxi for hire in comparatively thin line?

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
property to let is for hire

explanation.surface: A taxi available for hire waits in a fairly thin queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' suggests a queue for taxis; it is a rope, and the diminutive ending makes it a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cablet is a cable-laid rope of less than ten inches circumference, so a slimmer version of a full cable.

clue.text: Dies wretchedly after fall, once oedematous

indicators.note: something done wretchedly is done badly, so these letters come out wrong
after places the shuffled letters behind the word for fall

blocks.note: a drop is a fall
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dies miserably after a fall, having once been swollen with fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropsy is the old name for oedema, so dropsied is an obsolete word for swollen with fluid.

clue.text: Cultivated cordyline in reserve

indicators.note: in places the plant inside the word for reserve

blocks.note: to save is to reserve
the ti is a cordyline, a palm-like plant of the Pacific

explanation.surface: A garden plant is grown in a nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Sative is an old word meaning sown or cultivated, rather than growing wild.

clue.text: Anteater cross about e.g. worker density?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cross goes round what follows

blocks.note: a tau cross is T-shaped, named after the Greek letter
a man is an example of a worker, as in management and men
D is the symbol for density

explanation.surface: An anteater gets cross about a worker ant's density.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' alongside 'Anteater' suggests an ant; here it is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamandu, or tamandua, is a tree-dwelling anteater of Central and South America.

clue.text: Booby, one initially avoiding crush, tense

indicators.note: avoiding at the start means the word for crush loses the letter at its front

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the letter dropped
a crush, the person one is infatuated with, is an idol
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A fool, the one person who skipped the crush at first, is on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby is a stupid person, and a dolt is likewise a dull-witted fool.

clue.text: Urban company retains such money in accounts

indicators.note: retains means holds within, so the answer is held inside the words

blocks.note: letters held across the two words

explanation.surface: A city firm keeps cash on its books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such' points back to the hidden word's own sense: bank money, as opposed to currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Banco was bank money, the standard money of account at banks like Venice and Amsterdam, as against the depreciated coin in circulation.

clue.text: Canine? That's seen on golf club in Scotland perhaps

blocks.note: the letter C sounds like see; the setter uses it for what is seen
airn is the Scots word for iron, a golf club

explanation.surface: A dog is spotted on a Scottish golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The cairn terrier is a small Scottish breed, so the whole clue reads as a sort of &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a small, shaggy terrier bred in the Scottish Highlands, so it is one kind of dog.

clue.text: Primitive dwelling like a sieve, rate-free

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: cribrate means perforated like a sieve
the letters removed

explanation.surface: A primitive hut is full of holes, so no rates are paid on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib can be a hovel or rough hut, a basic dwelling, as well as a manger or child's bed.

clue.text: Grinder: one molar plays this role

indicators.note: plays suggests the letters perform in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written; it is an anagram of the answer plus the next word
the letters taken away from the shuffle

explanation.surface: A molar does its job as a grinder.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer together with 'role' is an anagram of 'one molar'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mano is a handheld stone used to grind maize or other grain against a metate.

clue.text: Street, old, with excellent porticos

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
O is a standard abbreviation for old
A1 means excellent, written with the letter I for one

explanation.surface: An old street boasts excellent colonnades.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoai is a plural of stoa, a covered colonnade or portico in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Henry's urgent call: 'Give us dinner with potato, properly prepared meat and eggs'

blocks.note: hall is dinner in a college dining hall
aloo is potato in Indian cookery
an alternative wordplay for the same letters, not needed once the first is used: hallal, a spelling of halal, plus OO for two eggs

explanation.surface: A posh diner shouts for a plate of dinner with potatoes, halal meat and eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter gives two routes to the same letters; the second splits after the sixth letter. The Henry is a Hooray Henry, a loud upper-class young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallaloo is a variant of halloo, a loud shout to attract attention or urge on hounds.

clue.text: Tortured victim under heartless Roman judges

indicators.note: heartless means its middle letter is removed
something tortured is twisted and wrenched out of shape, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
under with its middle letter gone

explanation.surface: A torture victim suffers under a cruel Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless Roman' looks like a cruel ruler, but heartless works on the word before it, and Roman belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The centumviri, literally a hundred men, were a court of judges in ancient Rome that heard civil cases.

clue.text: Rubbish, best in tabloids

blocks.note: Chambers lists red as a form of redd, rubbish
the tops is the very best

explanation.surface: A critic says the best journalism is found in rubbish tabloids.
explanation.walkthrough: Red-tops are British mass-market tabloid newspapers, named for their red mastheads.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular British tabloids such as The Sun carry red mastheads, so red-tops is the everyday nickname for them.

clue.text: Designs instruments for money?

blocks.note: first meaning: intends, as a verb
second meaning: methods or instruments, and also money or resources

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a single phrase about financial instruments; really it packs three senses: intends, methods, and wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for intends, as a noun for ways or methods, and as a noun for financial resources.
